why: the spin family, and its shape is the divergence. RESHAPED 2026-09-09 (phase-427) so the family carries upstream's names and only the RTOS-specific forms carry ours. `spin(SpinOptions) -> Result<(), NodeError>` is rclrs's name, argument and meaning: it was `spin_blocking`, because `spin` was squatted on by a `spin(Duration) -> !` task body with a different contract -- which made the rename the ONE porting edit on the rclrs tutorial's happy path that no real difference forced. Two bounds, both visible in the signature: rclrs returns `Vec<RclrsError>` and the caller writes `.first_error()?`, ours returns the FIRST error because there is no allocator (the edit is `.first_error()?` -> `?`), and `SpinOptions::poll_interval` is the quantum at which every exit condition is observed, because RFC-0002 makes this a poll loop. `spin_once(Duration)` is UNCHANGED and stays ours-only -- it drives I/O then dispatches EVERY ready arena entry (RFC-0002 section 3) where rclcpp's `spin_once` executes the next ONE, so the name matches and the meaning does not; see `cpp:Executor::spin_some`. `spin_some(max)` is NEW: rclcpp's drain verb, execute what is ready and return, never wait. `spin_forever(SpinOptions) -> !` is the former `spin`, renamed to say what it is -- a bare-metal entry has no shutdown source and nothing to return to, and `!` lets the compiler drop the epilogue; it absorbed `spin_default()` (0 call sites), whose 50 ms is now `SpinOptions::poll_interval`. `spin_period` / `spin_one_period` / `spin_one_period_timed` did NOT fold into `spin_some` and stay ours-only: they are RFC-0002's fixed-period dispatch, which PACES -- sleeps to an accumulated deadline so the rate does not drift -- and reports overrun, where `spin_some` executes what is ready, returns, and never sleeps. `spin_one_period` additionally RETURNS the remaining sleep for a caller with no clock to perform, which is not a value `spin_some`'s `Result` could carry. rclrs has no counterpart for any of the three: it spins as fast as work arrives.
